messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording for the Testing House’s review.

1. “The Testing House may use the drawings, including CAD geometry, solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel approved by the Design Owner by name and bound in writing by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance. The same conditions apply to advisers, subcontractors and replacement personnel.”

2. “The Testing House may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests, provided it encrypts them in storage and in transit. It may use the geometry to design and make fixtures dedicated to these tests. Fixture files and physical fixtures are subject to the same access and use restrictions as the drawings. The Testing House may not use the drawings, geometry or fixtures for another customer or to develop or assist in developing a competing product.”

3. “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the Testing House must securely erase the drawings and all working copies and derivative fixture files in its or its subcontractors’ possession or control, and physically destroy the derivative fixtures. It may retain a test report containing measurements and conclusions if the report does not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry.”

4. “Within the same 30 days, the Testing House must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier confirming destruction, identifying the categories of material covered and describing how and when the verifier confirmed destruction. This certificate satisfies the Design Owner’s verification requirement without a right of site access.”

Can your backup system meet the 30-day deadline, and does your accreditation require you to retain anything beyond the test report? If either requires an exception, please identify the material, the minimum retention period and who would need access so we can agree precise wording.

We accept clause 2. We can commit to the 30-day deadline for active files and physical fixtures. We have yet to confirm whether individual backup copies can be erased within 30 days. We also need to retain calibration records for two years. We can keep those records without drawing extracts or reconstructible geometry.

We propose two attachments and the following amendments.

1. **Clause 1 and Attachment A — recipients and extracts.** “Attachment A shall identify each approved external specialist by legal name and specify its task and permitted extracts. The machining shop may receive only the fixture manufacturing extracts it needs. The accredited lab may receive only the mounting and test setup extracts it needs. Within each approved organisation and the Testing House, access is limited to personnel assigned to the listed work, bound in writing by equivalent restrictions and recorded by name on an access register. The Testing House remains responsible for compliance.” We will supply the specialists’ names for approval before release. For a substitution, we propose written approval by email against the same attachment, with a response within three working days. The outgoing specialist’s access ends when its task ends, and it must confirm destruction of its copies within 30 days. The replacement receives extracts only after approval.

2. **Clause 3 and Attachment B — retention and disposal.** Add: “The Testing House may retain geometry-free calibration records for two years from the relevant test date, accessible only to personnel responsible for quality and calibration and, as needed for review, the accreditation assessor.” Before drawing release, we will confirm backup handling for each recipient in Attachment B. Where selective erasure is unavailable, we propose recording the actual maximum expiry period for your approval. Any such copy would be restricted to recovery administrators, expire through scheduled overwrite, and be erased again before restored data enter operational use. A recipient whose backup arrangements are still open receives no extracts.

3. **Clause 4 — verification.** “Within the clause 3 deadline, an authorised Testing House quality officer shall provide a signed certificate identifying the material categories, disposal methods and dates, supported by written confirmations from each specialist. The certificate shall identify any approved backup copies awaiting expiry and their scheduled expiry dates. The officer shall confirm final expiry in writing. If the Design Owner identifies a specific discrepancy that these records do not resolve, a mutually agreed independent verifier may review the relevant disposal records remotely under confidentiality. The verifier shall report its findings to both parties. Verification confers no right of site access.”

Would you accept the quality officer’s certificate as routine evidence, with independent review available for an unresolved discrepancy? We can provide a redacted access register and disposal log for that review while protecting other customers’ information.

Yes. We accept the quality officer’s signed certificate and each specialist’s written confirmation as routine proof of destruction. We also accept remote review of redacted records for a specific unresolved discrepancy, with no right of site access. Clause 2 is agreed.

We propose the following edits to close the remaining points.

1. **Attachment A.** We accept the proposed limits on extracts for the machining shop and accredited lab. Please add: “Before granting access, the Testing House shall submit each individual’s name, organisation, task and permitted material for the Design Owner’s written approval. It may submit a roster for approval in one email. Each approved individual must be bound in writing by equivalent confidentiality and use restrictions. The Design Owner shall respond to requests for additions or substitutions within three working days. Access begins only upon express written approval, including by email, and ends when the individual’s task ends.” An outgoing specialist’s 30-day disposal period runs from the end of its task, subject to any earlier deadline under clause 3 and any backup exception approved in Attachment B.

2. **Attachment B.** We accept two-year retention of geometry-free calibration records from the relevant test date, with access as you propose and deletion at the end of that period. We also accept scheduled overwrite where selective backup erasure is unavailable. Before release to each recipient, including the Testing House, Attachment B must record its maximum expiry period measured from the applicable disposal trigger, the names of any recovery administrators able to access the material, and the restore procedure you proposed. Those administrators must have equivalent written confidentiality and use obligations. Each exception requires our written approval before release. The quality officer shall confirm expiry to us in writing within five working days after each approved expiry date and promptly report any missed expiry.

3. **Clause 4.** To make the review available when needed, we propose: “If the Design Owner identifies a specific discrepancy and the disposal records and written clarifications do not resolve it, the Design Owner may require a confidential remote review. The parties shall promptly appoint a mutually acceptable independent verifier. The Testing House shall provide the relevant register entries, disposal logs and specialist confirmations. It may redact other customers’ information while preserving the names, dates and material identifiers needed to resolve the discrepancy. The verifier shall report its findings to both parties.”

If you accept those edits, the wording is agreed from our side. Please send Attachments A and B for approval before the first release.

We accept your edits to Attachments A and B and clause 4 as written. The wording is agreed. We will send both attachments for written approval before the first drawing release.

Attachment A will identify the machining shop and accredited lab by legal name and list each individual’s organisation, task and permitted material. We will use the same email approval process for substitutions during the job.

Attachment B will record the agreed calibration retention terms and each recipient’s verified backup arrangements, including our own. For any requested overwrite exception, we will provide the maximum expiry period measured from the applicable disposal trigger, the recovery administrators’ names and the restore procedure. The roster and backup details are still pending. Access will begin only after your express written approval covers the recipient, its personnel and any applicable backup exception.

One prototype drawing now includes export-restricted geometry on page 4. We request a narrow addendum so the rest of the vibration work can proceed under the agreed terms.

> For this drawing, the Design Owner shall supply a test copy with the page 4 geometry removed, including from any embedded CAD data. The Testing House and its specialists may use that copy within their existing approvals. Page 4 geometry and any extract or fixture file that reveals it are outside the approved release. For the affected test, the Testing House shall use a reference coupon supplied by the Design Owner once the coupon passes the verification test agreed in writing by both parties. Unaffected tests may proceed under the existing terms.

Our project engineer needs two days to prepare the coupon once we agree on verification. We propose mounting it in the intended fixture, running a low-level vibration sweep over the relevant test band and comparing the measured response with a geometry-free reference response we supply. Before the sweep, we would agree on the measurement locations, response metric and numerical pass limits. The Testing House would record the result, and the affected test would proceed only after a documented pass.

Would that comparison establish the mounting and vibration behaviour you need for the affected test? Please identify any adjustment you need to the verification method and whether the two-day preparation period fits your test schedule.

Yes, provided the comparison also checks mounting repeatability. We accept the redacted test copy and the exclusion of page 4 geometry from all releases. We propose adding the following wording for the affected test.

1. **Coupon custody and fixture preparation.** “The Design Owner retains ownership of the coupon and delivers it directly to the approved test lead at the Testing House. The lead shall log receipt, control access, and return the coupon directly to the Design Owner after the affected test or earlier termination. The coupon stays at the Testing House until return. The lead may measure the coupon there against mounting tolerances specified by the Design Owner. The shop may use its existing cut stock and receive only a tolerance table expressly cleared by the Design Owner for release to the named shop under Attachment A. The table must not disclose or permit reconstruction of page 4 geometry. Raw coupon measurements stay at the Testing House.” Please supply the mounting tolerances and identify the fields you can clear for the shop before it resumes machining.

2. **Verification and signoff.** “Before the first sweep, both parties shall approve in writing the mounting procedure, sweep band, measurement locations, response metric, numerical limits against the reference response, and maximum permitted difference between runs. The test lead shall run the sweep in the intended fixture, remove and independently remount the coupon using the same procedure, and repeat the sweep. Both runs must meet the reference limits and their difference must meet the repeatability limit. The lead shall sign the results and send a geometry-free verification record to the Design Owner’s project engineer. The affected test may begin on the engineer’s written confirmation of the pass. A failed check holds the affected test pending an agreed correction and repeat verification.”

3. **Timing.** We can accommodate the two-day coupon preparation period from written agreement on verification and will use that time for unaffected tests. The affected test will take the first available slot after coupon delivery, fixture readiness and written signoff. Can your engineer review the verification record on the day of receipt so we can reserve that slot?

We accept the coupon custody, two-run verification and scheduling terms. Our project engineer will review a complete geometry-free verification record on the day of receipt. Please agree a delivery time with the engineer when reserving the provisional slot. The affected test may start once the engineer confirms the pass in writing.

We propose the following wording for the shop release.

> The shop’s tolerance table may identify the coupon revision, a coupon-only datum label, the fixture feature to be machined, the dimension to be checked, its units, and its nominal value and tolerance or upper and lower limits. The Design Owner’s project engineer shall clear each populated row for the named shop before release under Attachment A. The shop may resume the affected machining only on receipt of the cleared table. Raw coupon measurements stay at the Testing House.

The numerical mounting tolerances are pending the coupon design. During the two-day preparation period, the engineer will supply the mounting acceptance limits directly to the approved test lead and issue the shop only the rows needed for machining that cannot disclose or permit reconstruction of the page 4 geometry. Please send the fixture features the shop needs to machine and the corresponding checks it needs to perform so the engineer can prepare that table.

We agree that both sweeps must independently meet the reference limits and that the difference between runs must meet the repeatability limit. Please send the proposed verification procedure and numerical limits for joint written approval. That approval starts the two-day preparation period.

We accept the shop-release wording. For the stock already cut, we propose the following feature and check pairs for the engineer to reconcile with the coupon design. Please issue only the rows that require machining.

| Fixture feature | Shop check |
|---|---|
| Coupon seating face | Flatness across the seating area |
| Locating face or stop, if used | Offset and perpendicularity to the cleared fixture datum |
| Fastener holes, if required | Hole diameter and position relative to the cleared fixture datums |

These are proposed checks pending confirmation against the actual fixture. The engineer will set the nominal values and tolerances and clear each populated row for the named shop. The test lead will check the finished fit against the coupon at the Testing House.

For joint approval, we propose measuring acceleration at the fixture input and at one engineer-designated coupon location along the excitation axis. Use the same locations, sensor orientation, fastener torque, sweep settings and frequency grid for both runs. Record the ratio of coupon acceleration amplitude to fixture input acceleration amplitude at each agreed comparison frequency. After the first run, fully release and reseat the coupon, retorque it and repeat the sweep.

We propose **±3 dB against the reference for each run and a maximum 1.5 dB difference between runs**, at every agreed comparison frequency. Use \(20\log_{10}\) of the amplitude ratio when calculating each difference. These are proposed acceptance limits. Please confirm they meet your test objective and supply the reference curve, comparison frequencies, sweep band, input level, sweep rate, sensor locations and mounting torque for the written procedure. A run with clipping or insufficient signal at a comparison frequency must be repeated before signoff.

Joint written approval of the completed procedure starts the two-day preparation period. When reserving the provisional slot, we will agree a delivery time for the verification record with your engineer so the affected test can start after same-day written confirmation of a pass.

We accept the proposed measurement method, full remount between runs and repetition of any run affected by clipping or insufficient signal. We agree to use ±3 dB against the reference for each run and a maximum 1.5 dB between runs as the proposed limits at every agreed comparison frequency. Our engineer will confirm their suitability when approving the reference curve and frequency grid. Please include a numerical minimum signal criterion for your measurement system in the procedure so the lead can determine whether a run is valid.

For joint written approval, our engineer will supply the geometry-free reference curve, comparison frequencies, sweep band, input level, sweep rate, sensor locations and mounting torque. The reference and each measured curve will use the same quantity, \(20\log_{10}(A_\text{coupon}/A_\text{input})\). The lead will compare the absolute differences in dB at each agreed frequency. The two-day coupon preparation period starts when both parties approve the completed procedure.

The seating face, locating stop and fastener holes are acceptable candidate features. The engineer will issue only the populated rows needed for the actual machining, after reviewing the table as a whole for disclosure of page 4 geometry. The test lead will check the finished fit against the coupon at the Testing House. Same-day review remains agreed for a complete verification record delivered at the scheduled time.

We propose adding this run-validity criterion to the procedure:

> Before each sweep, with the coupon mounted and excitation off, the test lead shall record the background RMS acceleration on both the input and coupon channels. The lead shall use the same gain, bandwidth, frequency grid and amplitude processing for the background and the sweep. At every agreed comparison frequency, each channel’s sweep RMS amplitude must be at least **10 times its own background RMS amplitude** at that frequency (20 dB). If either channel clips or falls below that threshold, the lead shall correct the measurement condition and repeat the full affected run. The verification record shall include each channel’s smallest measured margin in dB and the frequency at which it occurred for each run.

Please include this criterion with the engineer’s reference curve and sweep settings for joint written approval. That approval starts the two-day coupon preparation period.

We accept the run-validity criterion as written. Our engineer will include it with the geometry-free reference curve and sweep settings in the procedure for joint written approval. The two-day coupon preparation period begins when both parties approve the completed procedure.
